draft.title: Land degradation from farming
card: Land degradation is when farmland gets worse and can grow less. Farming can cause it when it is done poorly.
Soil erosion
wind and water carry away topsoil, the fertile top layer. Clearing plants and overgrazing leave bare soil, so it is easily blown or washed away.
Salinity
salt rising to the surface. Clearing deep-rooted trees can let the water table rise and bring salt up with it. Salty soil harms most crops.
Soil acidity
soil that becomes too acidic for many crops. It can build up over time with some farming practices, such as heavy use of certain fertilisers.
draft.remember: Clearing, overgrazing and poor practices can erode, salt or acidify soil, so it grows less.

a.q: A farmer in north-east Victoria clears all the trees from a sloping paddock. Heavy rain then washes away the topsoil. Which type of land degradation is this?
opts: Soil erosion
Salinity
Soil acidity
Overgrazing
a.why: Water carried away the topsoil, which is soil erosion. Overgrazing is a farming practice that can cause degradation, not a type of degradation itself, so it is the tempting wrong answer.

b.q: White crusts of salt appear on a wheat paddock in the Wimmera where the farmer cleared deep-rooted trees years ago. Why have crop yields fallen?
opts: Salt has risen to the surface and harms the crops
Wind has blown the topsoil away from the paddock
The soil has become too acidic for the crops
Too many sheep have eaten the plants on the paddock
b.why: White salt crusts show salinity. Clearing deep-rooted trees can let salt rise to the surface, and salty soil harms most crops. Erosion also lowers yields, but it removes topsoil and does not leave salt crusts.
b.clue: What do the white crusts on the soil show?

b.best: Salt has risen to the surface and harms the crops

problems.detail: The stem says 'White crusts of salt appear', and the right option is the only one that mentions salt. A student can match the word without knowing what salinity is or how clearing deep-rooted trees causes it. Describe the white crusts without naming salt, or ask about the cause instead.
